blindSummary:
This country is one of the region's safest and most progressive destinations for trans visitors. A 2018 comprehensive trans-rights law provides legal gender recognition by administrative self-declaration (no surgery or diagnosis required), a reparation pension for trans victims of institutional violence, and a state employment quota for trans people. Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2013 — a regional first — and bathroom access is legally protected.

The country is consistently placed among the region's safest by an international peace index, and a political-rights watchdog describes it as having strong democratic governance and a positive record on political rights and civil liberties. However, in July 2025 a 29-year-old trans woman was shot dead in her home in the capital (the assailant was sentenced to 7 years), and discrimination incidents have been documented at a public hospital and a state bank. The same watchdog notes disparities in the treatment of transgender people despite legal equality.

For a visitor: no border friction, bathrooms protected, no criminalisation, and the capital is welcoming.
blindOutOfScope: General crime is very low; no trans-specific travel advisory.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): broad protections - same-sex marriage since 2013, adoption since 2009, accessible legal gender recognition; since 2021 more than 120 trans people have accessed a reparation pension for institutional violence suffered during the 1973-1985 dictatorship; anti-discrimination law explicitly covers SOGI and hate-crime laws include SOGI aggravating circumstances.

A law school's legal resource on the 2018 comprehensive trans-rights law: ensures the right to a life free of discrimination and stigmatisation; the right to free development of personality per one's gender identity regardless of biological, genetic or anatomical factors; right to identification matching gender identity; includes reparation mechanisms.

Crowd-sourced safety data for the capital (governed by national law): homosexuality legal, marriage legal, gender change with no restrictions, gender-affirming care legal, full ban on intersex infant surgery, hate-crime protections cover SOGI, discrimination illegal, conversion therapy banned, bathroom access protected.

Official executive promulgation (Nov 2018): the comprehensive law for trans persons - the right to gender identity and a life free of discrimination, name/sex change on identity documents, and a reparation regime for trans people born before 31 December 1975 who suffered institutional violence or deprivation of liberty.

International political-rights assessment 2024: rated free (96/100) - historically strong democratic governance; disparities remain in treatment and political representation of women, transgender people, Afro-descendant residents and the small indigenous population.

International transgender-memorial project entry (July 2025): a 29-year-old trans woman was shot in the head at her home in a residential district of the capital; police hypothesised the attack targeted the man with her and she was a collateral victim; the perpetrator was sentenced to 7 years; the state expressed sorrow.

National daily (May 2024): a trans person reported mistreatment and discrimination at a public hospital - another trans woman, previously brutally beaten by a driver in a coastal resort town (prompting a pride mobilisation there), discussed the case with the health-centre director alongside a criminal complaint.

News site (Sept 2025): a trans woman in a discrimination lawsuit against a state bank denounces concealment of evidence - she says the bank did not deliver the main record requested by the prosecutor and that she lost her job after publicising the case.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Dec 2007): this country became the first in its region to recognise same-sex civil unions - the head of state signed the law granting cohabiting couples (5+ years) the same rights as married couples regardless of sex, gender identity or sexual orientation; the leadership of a major religious denomination attacked the validity of gay relationships.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2018 law's self-declaration legal gender recognition, reparation pension and state employment quota are resident-facing; the July 2025 killing of a 29-year-old trans woman and the hospital and bank discrimination incidents concerned residents.
blindTangential: Same-sex marriage legal since 2013 (a regional first) — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
